statements.status_notes: The crate appears in the image SBOM because the rust-analyzer package ships a scan of the whole Cargo.lock of the src/tools/rust-analyzer workspace in Rust 1.100.0 (376 crates), and that lock file lists every crate of the workspace, not only the ones compiled into the shipped rust-analyzer and rust-analyzer-proc-macro-srv binaries. GHSA-jh2m-fhpj-3vr7 (RUSTSEC-2026-0486) concerns the rustix::fs extended-attribute functions. rustix 1.1.4 is reachable in the lock file only through tempfile, which only proptest and rusty-fork depend on, and proptest is a dev-dependency of lib/smol_str (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.100.0/src/tools/rust-analyzer/lib/smol_str/Cargo.toml). Dev-dependencies are not built into the shipped binaries, and the lock edges from the rust-analyzer and proc-macro-srv-cli crates do not reach rustix or tempfile.

GHSA-jh2m-fhpj-3vr7 (RUSTSEC-2026-0486) is about the rustix::fs extended-attribute functions (getxattr, listxattr and their l and f variants) in rustix 1.0.0 through 1.1.5. rustix appears in the SBOM because the Cargo.lock of flux v0.201.0 lists it, but it is not compiled into Kapacitor. Its only dependent in the lock file is tempfile, which flux-core declares as an optional dependency that only its `doc` feature enables. Kapacitor builds libflux with `cargo build --release --no-default-features --features=cffi`, and flux v0.201.0 depends on flux-core with default-features = false, so `doc` is off. The amd64 kapacitord binary contains no symbols from the rustix or tempfile crate, while the crates that are compiled in (anyhow, chrono, libflate, parking_lot_core) do.
